newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate rises on bank borrowing.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate rises on bank borrowing.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate firmed back to 9.0 percent on Friday as banks covered their short positions, dealers said.
The overnight fell to 7.5/8.0 percent on Thursday after foreign banks, flush with funds, offered lower.
"Local banks were still short and were borrowing from 8.30 to as high as 9.0 percent," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
But the overnight rate was likely to be capped at 9.0 percent by Bank Negara, he said.
Dealers said interbank rates have remained firm in recent weeks due to tightness particularly at the short-end of the market.
But maturities of Bank Negara bills next week could improve market liquidity and pull rates slightly lower, they said.
"There will be two maturities worth 1.5 billion ringgit next week and this should help ease the market a bit," said a dealer.
There will be a new issue of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Tuesday.
Earlier, one- and two-week money were traded at 9.0 percent, unchanged from Thursday.
The one-month rate was at 8.0/8.5 percent and three-month money was at 8.0/8.3 percent, both about unchanged from previous.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were mixed.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down three points to 92.11, or an implied yield of 7.89 percent.
March 1998 contract was up three to 92.58, or 7.42 percent.
Futures dealers said the near month contracts were expected to face more selling pressure because of firm underlying interest rates.
